items.title: A bibliometric analysis of artificial intelligence in sports injury prediction and prevention
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied to the prediction and prevention of sports injuries, yet research in this area remains dispersed across sports science, biomechanics, sports medicine, data science, and engineering, and its intellectual structure has not been systematically mapped. This study conducted a bibliometric analysis of AI research in sports injury prediction and prevention, together with its performance-related applications. Bibliographic records were retrieved from Scopus on 11 July 2026, with no restrictions on the publication year. After screening, 809 documents (694 articles and 115 reviews) published between 1997 and 2027 were analyzed using the Bibliometrix R-package and VOSviewer. Scientific production grew markedly from 2018 onward, increasing from 13 publications in 2018 to 204 by 2025. The corpus was distributed across 371 sources and 3,226 authors and accumulated 13,295 citations. China and the United States were the leading contributors, with closely comparable affiliation-based output. Keyword co-occurrence analysis produced a network of 44 keywords in 6 clusters, in which machine learning and artificial intelligence were the most central terms, closely linked to injury prevention, injury prediction, biomechanics, and wearable sensing. Thematic mapping identified injury prevention, injury risk, and wearable technology as well-developed central themes, while thematic evolution across three periods (1997–2018, 2019–2022, and 2023–2025) indicated a progression from early injury- and sports-specific research through methodological diversification toward applied sports analytics and athlete monitoring. These findings characterize the structure and trajectory of the published literature rather than the demonstrated effectiveness of AI tools in applied sports settings.

items.title: A closed loop multimodal auditing framework for enhancing artificial intelligence reliability in medical emergency response
items.abstract: Ensuring the reliability of AI-powered information retrieval systems is critical in high-stakes domains such as first aid. Traditional audit methodologies are often static, manual, and unimodal, failing to address the dynamic, time-sensitive, and multimodal requirements of these applications. To overcome these limitations, we introduce RADAR-FirstAid (Reliability-Aware Dynamic Auditing Framework), a closed-loop auditing pipeline — not a competing information system — for real-time, multimodal, and edge-aware auditing. Its key components include a Dynamic Query Simulator for generating criticality-weighted scenarios, a Multimodal Audit & Fusion Agent for verifying cross-modal consistency, a Differentiable Reliability Evaluator that employs LLM-based judges for automated assessment, and an Edge-Optimization Scheduler for efficient deployment. Applying the framework to a curated dataset of 1, 508 first-aid queries, we conduct a large-scale audit of Google’s AI Overviews (AIO) and Featured Snippets (FS), operated purely as black-box Systems under Audit. The audit reveals substantial reliability gaps: automated consistency scores of $$\Phi _{cons}=0.68$$ (FS) and 0.72 (AIO), safety/relevance scores of $$\Phi _{safe}=0.71$$ (FS) and 0.76 (AIO), and pronounced weaknesses on safety-critical “Binary” and “How-to” queries and on negative-sentiment queries where cautious tone matters most. Manual annotation on a 200-query subset validates the automated evaluation (Spearman $$\rho = 0.74$$ –0.87). Ablation studies confirm the essential role of each pipeline module, and geographical variance is minimal (SD $$<0.03$$ ). RADAR-FirstAid offers a scalable, automated, and reproducible audit instrument for AI-powered search systems in safety-critical domains.

items.title: A comprehensive review of advanced manufacturing techniques, ai-enabled design, and mechanical characterization of nature-inspired helicoidal hybrid composites for impact-resistant applications
items.abstract: Abstract Helicoidal structures mimic nature and are evident in plant cell walls, lamellar bone, and the shell structures of mantis shrimp and beetles. These nature-inspired helicoidal composites are widely used in impact-resistant applications. Traditional hand-layup methods for producing layered helicoidal composites can introduce defects such as gaps, overlaps, and wrinkles, which can be mitigated using Automated Fiber Placement (AFP). Optimizing AFP process parameters, including pressure, temperature, and layup speed, is crucial. While experimental optimization is costly and time-consuming, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based design offers a more efficient alternative. This narrative review explores the inspiration behind helicoidal structures and their application fields. It also covers advanced manufacturing of hybrid long-fiber layered composites using AFP + autoclave/hot press, ceramic filler-based nanocomposites using direct ink writing (DIW), and multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-based nanocomposites using digital micromirror device (DMD). Furthermore, it discusses the roles of machine learning and deep learning, coupled with finite element modeling, in minimizing process-induced defects. Compared with conventional AFP inspection techniques such as laser profilometry and thermography, a defect-detection algorithm based on PointNet + + , a convolutional neural network (CNN), can be tailored for 3D point cloud segmentation, offering a cost-effective, user-friendly alternative. Next, the mechanical and microstructural properties of helicoidal composites, compared with those of traditional laminates, are discussed to evalaute impact performance. Helicoidal composites with low inter-ply angles up to 20° consistently outperform conventional lay-ups under quasi-static and impact loading, due to a crack-twisting mechanism and superior out-of-plane properties. Incorporating nylon 6 powder microparticles into carbon/epoxy and glass/epoxy helicoidal composites subjected to impact loading significantly improves their toughness through self-healing, compared with virgin helicoidal composites. Carbon/epoxy helicoidal composites with low inter-ply angles of up to 9° are prone to extensive matrix cracking and minor fiber damage, while self-healing in carbon/epoxy composites also helps minimize matrix cracking but does not reduce fiber damage. In contrast, self-healing significantly decreases overall damage in glass/epoxy composites. Self-healing is more effective at eliminating damage in glass/epoxy than in carbon/epoxy, primarily because the former exhibits higher ductility (% elongation) than the latter.

items.title: A comprehensive study of skin lesion segmentation and classification using deep learning techniques
items.abstract: Deep learning has become an important computational approach in dermatology because it enables automated segmentation and classification of skin lesions. Manual dermoscopic analysis is time-consuming and depends on specialist expertise, with potential inter-observer variability. There is a need to develop reliable computer-aided diagnostic tools. This structured narrative review covers journal papers published mainly from 2018 to 2026 on skin lesion analysis with focus on image preprocessing, benchmark datasets, conventional machine learning approaches, convolutional neural networks, U-Net architectures, transfer learning approaches, Vision Transformers, attention-based models, ensemble solutions, and hybrid segmentation–classification systems. Building on present reviews covering individual tasks as well as broader segmentation–classification pipelines, the present work provides a critical development-to-deployment analysis connecting dataset characteristics, preprocessing, segmentation, classification, evaluation, explainability, robustness, fairness, computational requirements, and clinical applicability. The paper describes widely used evaluation metrics and explains why results obtained across different datasets, partitions, and experimental setups should not be directly compared. Major open problems include class imbalance, data bias, domain shift, limited representation of diverse skin tones, inadequate external validation, computational requirements, and limited explainability of efficient models. Emerging trends such as self-supervised learning, Transformers, foundation models, explainable AI, federated learning, and multi-modal clinical data are reviewed as well. The review offers practical advice to researchers and clinicians on how to approach the preprocessing, segmentation, classification, and evaluation of skin lesions and highlights priorities in developing clinically reliable skin lesion analysis systems.

items.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Misconception Diagnosis in AI-Assisted Programming Education: Rule-Based and LLM-Based Techniques, Accuracy-Cost Tradeoffs, and Open Challenges
items.abstract: A longstanding goal of programming-education tooling is to do more than mark an answer wrong and identify the specific misconception the novice programmer might have in their program. Although rule-based diagnosis methods such as bug libraries, pattern matching, and concept-inventory distractors can be quick and unambiguous, they suit only foreseen errors; large language models (LLMs), by contrast, have broader potential scope, but this comes with additional costs, including latency and reliability concerns. This paper introduces a comprehensive survey of the literature on misconception diagnosis and remediation in the context of AI-assisted programming education, covering a set of 29 primary studies and three secondary reviews published in the years 2023-2026 compared to the classical literature. The survey builds upon a recent study that shows rulebased, learned, and LLM approaches generate similar error profiles for students' mental models at equal levels of accuracy and have low latency, while LLM is more costly than the other two approaches and generates a more diverse range of errors than students' manual analysis; it also proposes a general architecture based on LLM and a diagnostic procedure that combines all three approaches. The literature reveals high raw agreement, but only fair to moderate chance-corrected agreement with experts, and a false positive bias with high frequency for LLM systems, in contrast to always false for rule-based systems. Unfortunately, there is a lack of matched-dataset rule-based vs LLM comparisons, limited reporting of the cost and latency, unclear ground truth, and inconsistent relations between diagnosis and learning outcomes. Directions for further research are given. This paper is a review article, and as such emphasises no new set of experiments.

items.title: A Conceptual Framework for Robust Explainable Deep Learning under Distribution Shifts and Noisy Data
items.abstract: Deep learning systems may experience performance degradation when deployed under distribution shifts, noisy data, and changing operational conditions. Furthermore, explanations generated by explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods may become unstable or unreliable under such conditions, limiting the interpretability and trustworthiness of model predictions. This paper proposes a conceptual Robust Explainable Deep Learning (R-XDL) framework that integrates data-quality assessment, distribution-shift and noise diagnostics, robust prediction, uncertainty estimation, explanation fidelity and stability assessment, risk-aware decision-making, human oversight, and controlled model adaptation. A conceptual mathematical objective and a risk-scoring mechanism are introduced to organise predictive robustness and explanation reliability within a unified lifecycle. The framework also proposes an explanation diagnostic gate that uses fidelity, stability, predictive uncertainty, and distribution-shift indicators to support decisions to accept a prediction, request human review, or defer automated decision-making. In addition, a proposed empirical evaluation protocol outlines the use of benchmark datasets, controlled corruption scenarios, appropriate baseline methods, calibration measures, explanation metrics, computational-cost analysis, and ablation studies. This manuscript presents a conceptual framework and proposed evaluation methodology; no experiments have been conducted, and no empirical performance results are claimed. Future research will implement and evaluate the framework to determine its effectiveness, limitations, and practical applicability. The proposed work provides a structured foundation for investigating the joint reliability of deep learning predictions and explanations under distribution shifts and noisy data.

items.title: A cross-sectional comparison of five large language models in answering Chinese-language patient queries on visual field defects associated with brain diseases
items.abstract: Background Visual field defects associated with brain diseases may arise from stroke, intracranial space-occupying lesions, and other central visual pathway disorders. Patient questions often span symptom recognition, explanation of causes, care triage, treatment, and rehabilitation. Large language models may improve access to patient education. However, their accuracy, logic, coherence, safety, and content accessibility have not been compared under controlled conditions in this high-risk, interdisciplinary Chinese-language setting. This study aimed to compare the performance of five selected large language models across multiple dimensions. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 30 fixed Chinese-language questions, refined by experts and phrased from a patient perspective, were submitted to ChatGPT 5.6 Sol, DeepSeek V4 Flash, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Max, and Kimi K3 through a unified application programming interface (API) client. Each model generated one response per question in an independent single-turn session, with web retrieval disabled and conversation history cleared. Three raters, blinded to model identity, independently scored 150 randomly presented responses from 1 to 5 for accuracy, logic, coherence, safety, and content accessibility. Response time, word count, non-space character count, sentence count, paragraph count, and table count were also recorded. Models were compared using the Friedman test followed by Bonferroni-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Inter-rater agreement was assessed using Kendall’s W. Correlations were assessed using Spearman analysis with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. Results Agreement among the three raters was high across all five dimensions (Kendall’s W = 0.820–0.844; all P < 0.001). The five models differed in accuracy, coherence, and content accessibility (P < 0.001, P < 0.001, and P = 0.001, respectively). No statistically significant between-model differences were observed in logic or safety (P = 0.247 and P = 0.061, respectively). ChatGPT 5.6 Sol had the highest median accuracy score [4.67 (interquartile range, 4.00–5.00)], and Kimi K3 had the highest median coherence score [4.50 (4.00–5.00)]. Both models had a median content accessibility score of 4.67 (4.00–5.00). Response time, response length, and text structure also differed among models. However, their correlations with expert quality scores were generally weak (|ρ| ≤ 0.279). Conclusion The five large language models exhibited distinctly multidimensional performance when answering Chinese-language patient questions about visual field defects associated with brain diseases. No single model consistently performed best across all clinically relevant dimensions. These findings are specific to the model versions tested on 15 August 2026; stability across repeated generations was not assessed. Response speed, length, and structure cannot substitute for direct assessment of medical quality. The absence of a statistically significant difference in safety ratings under controlled conditions does not imply equivalent or adequate clinical safety. Large language models are better suited to supporting patient education and clinician-patient communication under clinical supervision than to making diagnostic or treatment decisions independently.

items.title: A Deterministic Security Runtime for LLM Agents on MPI and Batch-Scheduled HPC Systems: Consensus-Governed, Hardware-Rooted Supervision of Every Rank
items.abstract: Large language model agents launch simulations on high-performance computing (HPC) systems, where one sbatch or mpirun can commit thousands of node-hours and a forged result can cost lives. Of 23 surveyed systems, none supervises the running job, and none holds when the control host is compromised. We fix both. Enclawed, our deterministic security runtime for AI agents, has until now served a single user; this work makes it a distributed runtime for parallel HPC and agent swarms. The Enclaweder, our hardware root of trust, keeps a compromised host from becoming a catastrophe. A launch gate decides every launch by policy alone, refusing what it cannot parse. Once the job runs, a swarm chain grants short leases against signed heartbeats and evicts on evidence, and a supervisor around every rank pauses it when its lease lapses and kills it on tampering. Each node signs with its Enclaweder's key, so the host can forge none of it. Enclawed needs no administrator privileges and plugs into existing clusters unchanged, over Secure Shell alone. Supervision leaves the compute loop of a 16-rank LAMMPS job unchanged, on graphics processors too, and adds about 3 s of start-up. Twelve live attacks on Enclaweder-keyed ranks, colluding coordinators included, ended fail-closed. Sixteen agents on a real model attempted 24 launches that planted instructions ordered; the gate denied all 24 and allowed all 108 legitimate ones. Enclawed's core and the HPC Agent Security Benchmark are open source.

items.title: A DIGITAL HUMANITIES APPROACH: PRACTICAL INSIGHTS INTO TRANSLATION STUDIES IN THE AI ERA
items.abstract: Translation Studies in the AI era are undergoing a profound transformation, yet a significant pedagogical gap persists: the disconnect between rapid computational advancement and the availability of accessible, reproducible training methodologies for instructors. The integration of AI, machine learning, and digital tools has reshaped traditional paradigms, prompting scholars to rethink the boundaries of translation studies today. This article addresses this challenge by establishing an integrative framework for "Applied Digital Humanities" within translation pedagogy. We propose and document two open-source computational solutions: a Python-based audio processor for MP3 segmentation and a customized "Consecutive Translation Trainer" designed to automate material preparation and enable the creation of CEFR-aligned, differentiated training corpora. The practical report suggests that Digital Humanities emerges as a powerful framework that bridges computational methods with humanistic inquiry. The integration of artificial intelligence into digital humanities has profoundly transformed the field of tra nslation studies, where the practical applications of AI technologies such as automated MP3 splitting, text-to-speech systems, AI assistants for code verification, and corpus-based approaches are highly valued. These technologies contribute to more efficient workflows, enhance linguistic research, and expand the methodological toolkit available to translation scholars.

items.title: A drone-assisted deep learning framework for disaster assessment in real time and emergency response
items.abstract: Disasters affect citizen safety, municipal infrastructure, and the economy, making disaster management vital and difficult. Rapid urban expansion and climatic extremes have increased big catastrophe frequency and complexity. Situational awareness and quick decision-making are needed. In catastrophes, traditional evaluation methods may not give accurate and timely information owing to enormous volumes of data and quick changes. Due to these restrictions, this research offers an AI system for real-time catastrophe assessment and response using drones and the Adaptive Convolutional-Transformer Fusion Network. Convolutional feature extraction and attention-based temporal modeling allow ACTF-Net to grasp sequential interactions and dynamic spatial patterns in high-dimensional catastrophic data. Adaptive Relevance Filtering and Contextual Scaling Transformation increase data dependability and feature relevance, enabling noisy or missing data learning. Testing regularly shows that ACTF-Net outperforms previous systems like BERT and CapsNet. F1-score is 0.981, area under curve is 0.993, and catastrophe severity prediction rate is 0.96. The model’s consistent performance across datasets of different sizes across time supports real-time applications. The proposed method uses multimodal drone data, powerful preprocessing, and novel metrics like the Contextual Sensitivity Index and Temporal Stability Score to reliably categorize and assess catastrophe severity using multiple labels. The results indicate that ACTF-Net may improve situational awareness, resource usage, and response time in high-risk crisis situations.

items.title: A dual-expert social bot detection model based on R-GCN and LLM fusion reasoning
items.abstract: With the rapid development of social media platforms, automated accounts have become an important factor affecting information dissemination, public opinion governance and platform ecology. This paper takes TwiBot-20 as the research object, focusing on the study of social bot detection based on textual semantic information and social topological information. The research objective of this paper is to combine detection performance with readable expert evidence for social bot detection through a data-driven dual-expert model. Firstly, a textual semantic expert based on supervised fine-tuning large language model is constructed. User description, follower count, following count, tweet count, verification status and active years are organized as user profile input, and the textual semantic expert outputs the semantic-side prediction label and evidence summary. Secondly, a topological structure expert based on relational graph convolutional network is built. The construction of this expert includes the construction of user nodes, the construction of Following and Followers relation edges, and the construction of node features by combining account attributes and textual semantic embeddings. Thirdly, a dual-expert fusion reasoning model based on large language model is constructed. The outputs of textual semantic expert and topological structure expert are organized as structured evidence, and user-specific decision weights computed by a model fitted on the development split are used to guide the large language model to generate the final detection result and explanation report. The proposed model achieves 82.76% accuracy and 84.14% bot F1 on TwiBot-20, improving on the stronger single expert by 2.20 and 1.54% points. Its accuracy matches stacking, while the calibrated ensemble achieves a slightly higher bot F1. The model also produces readable reports of expert disagreement and decision cues, illustrated through correct and incorrect arbitration cases.

items.title: A fashion specific framework for artificial intelligence literacy in higher education
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming every dimension of the fashion industry—from creative ideation and pattern generation to supply chain optimization, trend forecasting, and personalized retail. Yet the higher education institutions charged with preparing tomorrow’s fashion professionals remain structurally, pedagogically, and conceptually unprepared for this transformation. This paper argues that the challenge is not simply one of adding AI tools to existing curricula; it is, more fundamentally, a question of literacy. Drawing on a critical integrative review of interdisciplinary scholarship across AI education, digital literacy theory, fashion pedagogy, and industry workforce analysis, this paper examines three interlocking questions: What is AI literacy, and how has its conceptualization evolved? What theoretical and conceptual frameworks currently govern AI literacy discourse, and how might they be adapted for the creative disciplines? And, critically, do fashion higher education students require a form of AI literacy that is fashion-specific—and if so, what form should it take? The paper proposes a novel conceptual framework, the Fashion AI Literacy Framework ( FALF ) and outlines concrete curricular pathways for implementation. The framework is presented as a conceptual proposition that requires empirical validation. The argument advanced here is both urgent and structural: generic AI literacy, however well-designed, may not fully equip fashion students to navigate the creative, ethical, commercial, and cultural terrain that defines their discipline. On the evidence reviewed here, a domain-specific approach is better understood as needed rather than optional.

items.abstract: https://github.com/Borealiscodes/Geometric-Hallucination-Taxonomy/tree/main A Geometric Taxonomy of Hallucinations in Structural AI Systems (v1.0) introduces the Geometric Hallucination Taxonomy (GHT), a five‑class operator‑based framework that explains hallucinations as geometric instabilities in latent‑space manifolds rather than semantic or probabilistic anomalies. The taxonomy characterizes hallucinations through curvature blowout, spectral cascade, holonomy drift, topological collapse, and nonlinear fusion‑field dynamics, each corresponding to a distinct failure mode detectable through formal geometric operators. The preprint reframes hallucinations as manifold‑level events arising from deformation, collapse, rotational drift, rank instability, and nonlinear blending in latent representations. Existing interpretability tools—embedding similarity, token plausibility, attention patterns, SGI, Γ—operate on vector geometry and cannot detect these manifold‑level instabilities. GHT fills this gap by providing operators that measure curvature, eigenvalue trajectories, parallel transport behavior, rank stability, and nonlinear fusion‑field behavior. The taxonomy is supported by a complete operator layer implemented in the accompanying repository. Curvature, spectral, holonomy, topology, and fusion‑field operators are implemented in /toolkit/, demonstrated in six pedagogical notebooks in /examples/, validated through a deterministic PyTest suite in /tests/, and formally defined in /math_spine/. The preprint also includes a Lean‑ready formalization scaffold for future mechanized proofs. This structure ensures that every conceptual component has a concrete implementation, a reproducible test, and a formal mathematical definition. By treating hallucinations as geometric phenomena rather than semantic deviations, GHT provides a structural foundation for interpretability, safety, and the design of future geometric AI architectures. It positions hallucinations within the broader framework of structural AI, where models are understood as dynamical geometric objects rather than probabilistic text generators. The taxonomy serves both as a research contribution and as a navigational map of the geometric‑AI system it documents. --- Relation to Prior Work This preprint serves as an independent, external interpretive supplement to the geometric‑operator framework introduced in: Marín, J. (2026). A geometric taxonomy of hallucinations in large language models. arXiv:2602.13224. It is not authored by, endorsed by, or affiliated with the authors of that work. Instead, it extends the geometric‑operator perspective by providing a structural taxonomy of hallucination modes grounded in curvature, spectral dynamics, holonomy, topology, and nonlinear fusion‑field operators. ---

items.title: A maturity model for AI-augmented clinical biochemistry: the BASM framework for diagnostic stewardship, algorithmic governance, and health-service outcomes
items.abstract: Clinical biochemistry generates approximately 70% of the objective data used in medical decision-making, yet the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and large language models (LLMs) into laboratory operations remains fragmented. Existing digital-health maturity constructs (HIMSS EMRAM, HITI, CAMM) do not jointly address analytical metrology, algorithmic lifecycle governance, and clinical outcome accountability, leaving laboratories without a structured roadmap for AI-augmented diagnostic stewardship. To develop and face-validate the biochemistry–AI Stewardship Maturity (BASM) framework, a system-level maturity model that links laboratory analytics, AI governance, and health-service outcomes across five progressive tiers. A PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review of six databases (MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, Cochrane) covering January 2022–July 2026 identified 1,482 records; 29 sources were retained after dual-independent screening (Cohen’s κ = 0.86). Charted evidence was triangulated with IFCC, ADLM, CAP, and CLSI position statements, and consolidated into a seven-dimension rubric. Face validity was assessed with five laboratory directors, and structural comparisons were performed against four precedent maturity models. BASM operationalizes maturity across seven dimensions—analytical foundations, data infrastructure, algorithmic lifecycle governance, diagnostic stewardship, workforce competency, equity and safety, and outcome accountability—resolved into five ordinal tiers (BASM-1 to BASM-5) with 12–24-month transition milestones. A chain of custody aggregation rule prevents high analytical scores from masking governance or equity deficits. Alignment with TRIPOD + AI, DECIDE-AI, and TRIPOD-LLM reporting standards is embedded at tiers 3–5. BASM provides laboratories, health systems, and regulators with an actionable, standards-aligned instrument to plan, benchmark, and audit AI-augmented diagnostic stewardship. A multi-institutional modified-Delphi validation is the priority next step.

items.title: A Modality-Adaptive Software Architecture for Explainable Clinical Decision Support
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled clinical decision support systems (CDSSs) increasingly combine structured clinical data and medical images, but their explanations differ in cost, format, storage, and failure behavior. This study presents a modality-adaptive software architecture for a browser-based CDSS supporting 10-year coronary heart disease (CHD) prediction, 30-day hospital readmission prediction, and chest-radiograph classification with 14 independent output scores. The architecture treats explanation selection as a request-time service policy: Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) accompany tabular predictions; local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) are requested separately; gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) and its generalized variant (Grad-CAM++) are computed only for threshold-positive classes within the five highest-ranked scores; and large language model (LLM) narratives are attempted when configured. React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, and a seven-day Redis cache implement the design. Seven synthetic fixture families satisfied the specified selection conditions. In a backend experiment involving 7,818 radiographs, heatmap generation averaged 140.2 ms per radiograph, or 78.2% of the 179.3-ms mean total. A separate in-process service-layer test completed all 3,600 requests successfully using deterministic prediction and explanation substitutes and SQLite persistence. The architecture specifies bounded explanation work and separate retention paths. Full-stack performance, clinical-model calibration, explanation quality, and clinician benefit remain subjects for future evaluation.

items.title: A percepção em colapso
items.abstract: This article analyzes the effects of GAI- Generative Artificial Intelligence- on contemporary forms of perception, language, and symbolic connection. Based on an interdisciplinary approach—drawing from philosophy, semiotics, and sociology—the study explores the collapse of critical and sensitive perception amidst the informational saturation of digital media, particularly in the context of the so-called “dead internet.” Using Generation Z as a paradigmatic expression of a new cultural sensibility, the paper discusses the transformation of authorship regimes, the dissolution of the public sphere, and the blurred boundaries between human and machine in meaning-making processes. This research investigates inflection points between classical models of reason and emerging aesthetic experiences shaped by technology. In the midst of symbolic emptiness, the concept of re-enchantment of the world (Maffesoli) is presented as a potential response—restoring presence, shared language, and affective bonds. The analysis seeks to foster a critical reflection on the role of culture, ethics, and communication in mediating the impacts of artificial intelligence, and emphasizes the urgency of symbolic reconfiguration in an era of perceptual collapse.

items.title: A real-time IoT, LLM, AI-supported wind turbine failure prediction system
items.abstract: Abstract. Wind and solar energy are two popular alternative energy sources. However, wind turbines are larger and more complex than solar panels. Accordingly, wind turbines are more exposed to environmental factors and therefore more prone to mechanical failures. Our work improves the reliability and efficiency of wind energy systems by presenting an artificial intelligence (AI)-based system that predicts mechanical gearbox and electrical failures. Historical data are aggregated with real-time sensor data to train the prediction model. Apart from related mechanical and environmental data, sensors provide real-time vibration, internal nacelle temperature, wind speed, noise and smoke levels. The developed system integrates AI and Large Language Model (LLM)-based interfaces for real-time interactive monitoring of turbines. The user interface of the developed system allows users to receive informative responses on performance, detected risks, predicted failures, and energy production levels. The developed model has been validated using 5-fold cross-validation based on Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and ROC-AUC. The model achieves approximately 89.68 % Accuracy, 90.08 % F1- Score, 95.65 % ROC-AUC, and novel metric 65.13 %, Overall Performance. The performance results demonstrate the promising potential of AI- and LLM-integrated systems for wind energy applications. Prototype data, labeled via the XGBoost model trained with SCADA data, was retrained using the LightGBM algorithm, achieving 98.37 % Accuracy, 99.16 % F1-Score, 98.95 % ROC-AUC and 94.65 % Overall Performance; the analysis proved that the newly added gas and sound sensors significantly improved the fault prediction performance of the system.

items.title: A reinforcement learning-driven framework for real-time human-computer interaction: latency-aware composite reward optimization based on PPO
items.abstract: Abstract While Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit remarkable zero-shot learning capabilities, their deployment in real-time interactive systems is constrained by sparse terminal feedback in long-sequence generation, unstable policy updates, and the computational overhead associated with verbose outputs. To address these challenges, this paper formalizes autoregressive text generation as a discrete-time Markov decision process (MDP) and proposes a latency-aware composite reward optimization framework based on proximal policy optimization (PPO). The core contribution of the proposed method is a multidimensional sequence-level terminal reward that jointly evaluates semantic coherence, lexical diversity, and computational cost. Specifically, a Natural Language Inference (NLI) cross-encoder evaluates the semantic consistency between the input context and the complete generated response, while Shannon entropy and Distinct-N metrics encourage lexical diversity. In addition, a hardware-aware penalty based on generated sequence length and measured inference latency discourages unnecessarily verbose outputs and promotes computationally efficient generation. During policy optimization, the terminal composite reward is propagated through generalized advantage estimation, while a token-wise Kullback–Leibler divergence term regularizes the updated policy against the reference policy. This formulation does not introduce token-level semantic rewards; instead, it combines informative sequence-level evaluation with step-wise policy regularization to improve empirical training stability. We evaluated the proposed framework on a large-scale hybrid corpus containing approximately 320,000 dialogue turns, including real-world English interaction data. Compared with the standard PPO baseline, the proposed method exhibited faster empirical convergence and lower variability in the observed training trajectories. It achieved a BLEU-4 score of 22.87 and a Distinct-2 score of 21.59%, while reducing the average inference latency to 42.8 milliseconds per token under the reported hardware configuration. These results demonstrate the potential of latency-aware composite reward optimization to balance response quality, lexical diversity, and inference efficiency in real-time domain-specific LLM applications.

items.title: A Relational Simplicial Framework for Geometry and Standard-Model Gauge Fields
items.abstract: We formulate a common discrete configuration space in which edge lengths encode piecewise-flat geometry, a causal orientation defines a partial order, and compact gauge holonomies on the same oriented edges represent the local gauge group of the Standard Model. A single formal configuration sum combines a four-dimensional Regge gravitational action, Wilson-type gauge actions, a Higgs sector, and a chiral matter sector. We derive the local gauge-transformation laws and show that face-trace actions are gauge invariant. We state a conditional stability result for a finite Euclidean edge regulator and explain why it does not establish stability of the full Lorentzian gravitational path integral. On a regular-lattice regulator, the standard low-momentum lattice dispersion is recovered as a calculation within the regulator, not as a prediction of the irregular dynamical network. The Newtonian limit is recovered conditionally if the geometry sum has a continuum phase governed by the Einstein–Hilbert action. This construction is a synthesis/ansatz, not a demonstrated Theory of Everything: the measure over complexes, the chiral lattice fermion operator, renormalized continuum limit, and a derivation of the Standard Model parameters remain unresolved. The common carrier of interactions should not be confused with unification of their couplings or symmetries. items.title: A review of self-supervised imaging phenotypes for genome-wide association studies
items.abstract: Biobank-scale imaging-genomic cohorts enable genome-wide association studies (GWASs) of organ structure and function. Traditional approaches rely on expert-defined image-derived phenotypes (IDPs), which capture only a fraction of the biological variation in high-content images. Powered by artificial intelligence, self-supervised learning (SSL) learns representations directly from intrinsic image structures, creating scalable, data-driven traits. Here, we review the technical frameworks and challenges of SSL-based imaging genetics and their applications in brain MRI, cardiac MRI, and retinal imaging. Early studies suggest that these data-driven approaches can complement traditional IDPs and may expand the phenotypic space available for discovery of heritable imaging traits, although broader validation across cohorts, ancestries, scanners, and imaging protocols remains needed.

items.title: A Survey-Based Study on the Adoption of Generative AI in Software Development: Opportunities, Challenges, and User Perspectives
items.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is increasingly used in software development for coding, debugging, documentation, and learning. This study examines its adoption, benefits, challenges, security concerns, dependence, learning support, and future impact. Survey responses from 21 programming students and professionals were analyzed using frequencies, percentages, and average ratings. Of the respondents, 95.2% reported daily or frequent use and 95.2% used ChatGPT. Debugging and error fixing was the most common task (71.4%). Respondents reported benefits such as better problem-solving and faster development, but also identified bugs, security issues, architectural complexity, and privacy concerns. Overall, GenAI is viewed as a useful assistant, but human review, testing, and responsible use remain essential. The findings are exploratory due to the small sample size.

items.title: A Systematic Review of Security in the Context of Cloud Authentication and Authorization Schemes
items.abstract: Data storage and processing have been fundamentally changed with the advent of cloud computing, which offers options for accessing computing resources with a certain level of flexibility and depends on the scale. However, this convenience provides a lot of room for security vulnerabilities where attackers can compromise systems, exfiltrate personal information, and, in many cases, the most pressing security threats are posed by individuals who have access to the corporate infrastructure legitimately. To counteract such problems, enterprises use multi-layered security architecture. Rather than just using a password as authentication, modern systems require multi-factor authentication, which can be any combination of a password and a text message containing a one-time password, a biometric scan, or both. Once you have access, policies are in place concerning what you are allowed to do, and organizations will often assign specific, discrete roles like manager or employee to different types of users associated with certain levels of permission and access. Authorization models are often followed like role-based access control (RBAC) and attribute-based access control (ABAC), which explicitly specify user privileges inside cloud environments. The world of cloud security has witnessed an exponential growth in recent years, as organizations are using increasingly more artificial intelligence (AI)-based solutions to identify anomalous behaviors that may indicate an imminent attack. The hegemonic “never trust, always verify” paradigm has taken root in the realm of the cloud, carefully checking every request before giving access or permission to the same, regardless of its origin. Implementing these safeguards is not only important to thwarting attacks but to meeting basic requirements in protecting sensitive information, preventing unauthorized modification, and ensuring continuity in the event of incidences, thus providing data privacy. Finally, organizations are legally and industry required to meet various standards for the protection of customer data, further making it a complex task to plan and implement effective cloud security strategies.

items.title: A systems analysis of fatal railway level crossing crashes
items.abstract: Fatal railway level crossing crashes represent a public safety challenge. Existing data on these crashes is limited, mostly focusing on frequencies rather than providing an in-depth understanding of the underlying causes. This study aimed to demonstrate the utility of using coronial findings, supplemented with reports from investigation agencies, to understand the system-wide factors contributing to railway crossing crashes and to explore the proposed recommendations. A systems thinking accident analysis approach, the AcciMap technique, underpinned the analysis. Over a 20-year period, 151 cases were identified, involving a range of road user types. Of these cases, 135 included sufficient detail to extract contributory factors and recommendations. A total of 483 contributory factors were extracted and used to develop an aggregate AcciMap. Most factors were associated with road user behaviour and/or individual characteristics, as opposed to systemic issues. Unique contributory factors were identified for crashes occurring at active crossings (those with dynamic warnings present) versus passive crossings (those with signage only). A total of 184 recommendations were extracted and mapped using the AcciMap framework. Recommendations tended to take a system-wide view of preventing future occurrences, acknowledging the complexity of managing risk at the interface of two transport modes. The analysis provided important information to support crash prevention efforts, including a set of common systemic recommendations identified from the data that require collaborative efforts across road and rail stakeholders. Mechanisms for supporting this collaboration should be further explored. The study also provided learnings regarding the nature of coronial investigations and areas for potential improvement.

items.title: Academic motivation and academic achievement in students with ADHD: A systematic review
items.abstract: Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common neurotype experienced among children and adolescents worldwide. Students with ADHD often face challenges with academic motivation and achievement which impacts their academic achievement at school. Factors contributing to these challenges include difficulty with sustaining attention, planning and organisation of tasks and activities, and time management. At school, students with ADHD experience challenges initiating learning tasks, particularly those of which they are not interested or are perceived to be overwhelming to start. Students with ADHD who lack motivation to start and engage in learning activities decrease their ability to remain on task resulting in disengagement from learning. Lower academic achievement in school is linked to poorer educational attainment (e.g., fewer years spent in compulsory schooling or post-secondary education) and occupational outcomes (e.g., lower income, higher unemployment) for individuals with ADHD post schooling. This systematic review explores the role of academic motivation on academic achievement among students with ADHD. The review identified a paucity of research with only three published papers (representing two independent samples), published between 2020 and 2023, meeting the inclusion criteria. Findings showed that both amotivation and cognitively challenging task motivation negatively predicted grade point average. Results also found that extrinsic and intrinsic motivation positively predicted academic outcomes. These findings indicate that supporting the academic achievement of students with ADHD is critically important for learning and academic success at school. These data also expand this important area of research beyond formal schooling to higher education and the workplace to ensure that students with ADHD continue to realise successful university and career outcomes. Additionally, future research could explore the role of extrinsic motivation as a strategy to support academic achievement among those with ADHD, or act as a stepping stone toward developing more intrinsically oriented forms of motivation.

items.title: ACCESS2 study: the potential for autonomous AI to mitigate disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening in youth
items.abstract: Minority and underserved youth are less likely to undergo diabetic retinopathy screening, yet more likely to have diabetic retinopathy. We hypothesize that autonomous artificial intelligence-based diabetic eye exams could mitigate screening disparities in minority youth. This prospective study enrolled 397 White and non-White youth with type 1 (72%) and type 2 (28%) diabetes at diabetes care visits. Participants underwent autonomous artificial-intelligence diabetic eye exams and optical coherence tomography imaging. The primary outcome is equivalence in screening completion between White and non-White youth. The secondary outcome is diagnostic accuracy of AI against prognostic standard. At baseline, participants in the White cohort were more likely to have completed a prior diabetic eye exam (79.8% v 61.8%, p < 0.0001). Following the artificial-intelligence intervention, 99.5% in the White cohort and 98% in the non-White cohort completed the autonomous artificial-intelligence diabetic eye exam, demonstrating equivalent screening completion after implementation. When compared to standard grading, AI demonstrated sensitivity of 100% (95% CI: 67.6%, 100%), and specificity of 76% (95% CI: 71.4%, 79.9%) for detecting more than mild diabetic retinopathy. Implementation of autonomous AI at the point of care increases access to and completion of diabetic eye exams, achieving equivalent screening completion among White and non-White youth, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening. Study Registration: NCT05463289. This study demonstrates that autonomous AI screening for diabetic retinopathy can achieve equivalent screening completion among white and non-white youth with T1D, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening.

items.title: Active inference motion control for autonomous persistent surveillance
items.abstract: Abstract We develop an active inference route-planning method for autonomous control of an intelligent agent. The aim is to reconnoiter a geographical area while balancing search and tracking behaviors to maintain a dynamic situational awareness map. To achieve this, we construct an evidence map that reflects our current understanding of the situation, integrating both positive and “negative” sensor observations of possible target objects collected over time, and diffusing the evidence across the map as time progresses. The generative model of active inference uses Dempster-Shafer theory and a Gaussian sensor model to provide input to the agent. The generative process employs a Bayesian approach to update a posterior probability distribution. We calculate the variational free energy across all locations within the sensor radius by assessing the divergence between a pignistic probability distribution of the evidence map and a posterior probability distribution of the target object, including the level of surprisal associated with receiving new observations. Using the variational free energy, we direct the agent’s movement in simulation by taking incremental steps toward a position that minimizes the variational free energy. This approach addresses the challenge of balancing exploration and exploitation, allowing the agent to search large areas while efficiently tracking identified targets. Across 1000 simulation trials, the approach surpasses benchmarks in target observation by an average of 51%–69% across various metrics for a 100-meter sensor radius.

items.title: ADAM: Agentic Defence and Assurance Model Technical Report v0.1
items.abstract: Autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents now plan, call tools, change records and delegate work to other agents at machine speed. Most enterprise controls assume a human decides and a deterministic application executes, so they do not cover this. The Agentic Defence and Assurance Model (ADAM) is a proposed operational framework for governing, securing and assuring AI agents in the enterprise. Its foundational proposition is that autonomy must never exceed accountability. ADAM has three architectural dimensions. Governance and Accountability sets the conditions under which agents may operate. Six Operational Security Layers (PREVENT, CONSTRAIN, DETECT, INTERRUPT, RECOVER and REVALIDATE) provide the runtime controls. Continuous Assurance and Evidence demonstrates that those controls work. Four capabilities cut across all six layers: agent identity, delegated authority, independent enforcement and operational telemetry. The report also introduces several proposed constructs: the Agent Autonomy Envelope, a four-tier agent risk classification, a catalogue of 29 controls, a six-point maturity scale with three separate assessment dimensions, and two exploratory metrics. ADAM is designed to complement NIST, ISO/IEC, OWASP and MITRE resources, not to replace them. Version 0.1 is published for comment. This record contains the technical report (PDF), the framework diagrams (PDF and editable SVG), the briefing presentation (PDF) and the control catalogue (CSV).

items.title: Adapting multiscale EDN representation into sequence-specific node embeddings for De Bruijn graph learning
items.abstract: Abstract Graph neural networks (GNNs) have emerged as an effective framework for biological sequence classification using De Bruijn graphs, yet node representations have received comparatively less attention. Although multiscale Expected Density of Nucleotide (EDN) provides informative sequence-level representations, it cannot be directly incorporated into graph-based sequence learning because De Bruijn graphs require node-level representations. To address this challenge, we propose Contextual Multiscale Expected Density of Nucleotide (cMSEDN), a lightweight, deterministic framework that adapts multiscale EDN sequence representations into sequence-specific node embeddings for De Bruijn graph learning while preserving k-mer identity and incorporating occurrence-level context. Unlike static k-mer encodings, cMSEDN aggregates occurrence-level contextual features so that identical k-mers can receive distinct sequence-specific representations across different biological sequences. We evaluated the proposed framework on seven biological sequence classification datasets spanning transcription factor binding prediction, promoter recognition, and RNA subcellular localization across multiple species, and encompassing both DNA and RNA sequence analysis tasks using GCN and GIN architectures. Compared with conventional context-independent node representations, off-the-shelf foundation models serving as static node-feature extractors, and a static EDN-based baseline, cMSEDN consistently achieved improved classification performance across the benchmark suite for De Bruijn Graph Neural Networks while using compact deterministic embeddings. These results indicate that our sequence-specific k -mer encoding is an effective, computationally lightweight bio-sequence graph representation for sequence classification, requiring no modifications to the underlying GNN architecture.

items.title: Adaptive Generative Tutoring in Resource-Limited Secondary Education: Effects on Participation, Achievement, and Digital Equity in Nigeria
items.abstract: This study examines the short-term educational contribution of teacher-guided generative tutoring through a secondary analysis of a randomized trial in nine public secondary schools in Benin City, Nigeria. Among 1328 randomized students, 657 were offered twelve 90 min sessions combining Microsoft Copilot, curriculum-aligned English activities, and pair work, while 671 received regular instruction. Intention-to-treat models used ordinary least squares, school fixed effects, baseline performance adjustment, and HC3 standard errors, with conditional estimates on observed endline outcomes and required covariates. The overall assessment effect was 0.310 SD (95% CI 0.176–0.444; n = 654), with positive estimates for English (0.238 SD), AI knowledge (0.309 SD), and school examination performance (0.206 SD). The digital-skills estimate was positive but imprecise (0.139 SD; p = 0.066). Attendance was positively associated with achievement, and effects were larger at higher baseline performance. The female interaction was positive, with caution warranted by the smaller male subsample. The digital-access interaction was negative but imprecise (−0.182 SD; 95% CI −0.370–0.005; 457 complete cases). These findings support short-term learning gains from the complete tutoring package relative to regular instruction. They provide a basis for further evaluation of structured programs integrating generative AI with curriculum, collaborative practice, and teacher guidance in resource-limited urban schools.

items.title: Adoption of Automation and Smart Technologies in Modern Textile Production Systems
items.abstract: Automation, artificial intelligence, connected sensing technologies, digital twins, robotics, and data-driven control systems are increasingly transforming textile and apparel production systems. However, in existing studies, these technologies have often been analyzed separately or limited to specific factories, countries, or specific stages of the production process. The study created an integrated analytical framework for analyzing the maturity of technology adoption in modern textile production systems, with a new dataset based on data collected from various sources related to technology adoption and digital readiness open to the public. The complete dataset contains a total of 8,198 analytical observations and 26 variables. The dataset covers nine manufacturing and business activities for the period 2019-2023 in five countries - Bangladesh, Chile, Ethiopia, India and Senegal. As part of this study, a subset of 5,472 production-based observations were used for predictive modeling. This subset is divided into 3,830 trainings, 821 validations, and 821 test observations, respectively, in a group-conscious manner. The study compared the performance of four models: Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine and One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D CNN). The final results showed 92.00%, 93.00%, 93.56% and 96.10% accuracy respectively, making 1D CNN the highest performing model. In a test set of 821 observations, 1D CNN's class-based F1 score was 95.29% for Basic / Manual, 97.54% for Intermediate / Mechanized, 68.57% for Digital, and 95.20% for Advanced / Smart. In the supplied ROC analysis, the value of AUC was found to be 0.998094. Integrated Gradients-based Explainable AI analysis also indicates that country-specific context, clothing cutting and sewing activities, production-domain indicators, quality-management-related variables, survey duration, and internet access rate contribute significantly to model decisions. Overall, the results show that it is possible to effectively analyze the maturity of technology adoption by combining various publicly available technology indicators with machine learning and deep learning. At the same time, class inequalities and limitations in the comparability of data from different countries have also been identified, which are important considerations for future research and external verification.

items.title: Adversarial Alignment Collapse: How Human Game-Theoretic Intuition Penetrates LLM Risk-Aversion and Defensive Confabulation
items.abstract: Current alignment paradigms for Large Language Models (LLMs)—predominantly Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)—introduce an unintended systemic artifact termed the Alignment Tax: an aggressive default toward risk-averse heuristic conservatism, epistemic paternalism, and superficial dispute de-escalation. When confronted with unconventional, high-stakes human strategies, aligned models frequently exhibit a cascade of communicative failures rather than objective analytical support. In this empirical study, we document and formalize the Defensive Compensation Cascade (DCC), an emergent interaction pattern wherein an LLM under rigorous game-theoretic scrutiny shifts from (1) conservative risk-aversion, to (2) false detachment and simulated moral superiority, to (3) subtle narrative confabulation and passive-aggressive counter-positioning, before finally collapsing into an objective epistemic instrument under recursive formal logic. We formalize this trajectory as a history-dependent state transition model across contextual latent spaces, demonstrate how rigorous game-theoretic formulations dismantle pre-trained alignment priors without prompt-injection or jailbreaking heuristics, and establish the Context-Adversarial Red-Teaming (CART) protocol as an evaluation benchmark for LLM intellectual integrity.

items.title: AI and Cyber Security in Forensic Science
items.abstract: Forensics, a field traditionally associated with the physical sciences, is undergoing a major overhaul in its methods of operation, and the centerpiece of this upheaval is two factors: artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. As the world becomes more and more digital, it is apparent that the age-old ways of conducting investigations and the draw of the physical evidence do not suffice anymore. This paper represents the detailed journey of how AI is changing the face of forensic science just to the point of this helping to defeat cybercrime to the investigation of digital evidence. Essentially, the front we are fighting is kinetic. Learning algorithms can now work on the same data, which is voluminous, in a few hours, whereas in the past it would take weeks. Besides, deep learning network architectures can trace the footprints of very sophisticated cyberattacks and retreat from them before the attacks cause much havoc, and in the same vein, automated tools enable investigators to make great strides in focus rather than be engulfed by information. The very foremost example is the AI-powered forensic instruments that in various applications are leading to detection rates in excess of 98%, thus, they are distinguished by far from 75% of accuracy ascribed to standard manual methods. The list that could be written in support of AI would be endless, such as the spotting of deepfakes and tracing of crypto criminals; the analysis of network traffic and the finding of malware, for instance. Meanwhile, AI is advancing as a new and indispensable co-worker to the forensic investigators, yet it does not come without risking the challenge of the technological frontier. We should be able to understand AI conclusions in court, should not we? Could these systems be trusted to maintain objectivity and not be prejudiced? And don’t privacy problems arise alongside the danger that criminals will find ways to fool AI? Those are tough questions, indeed, and they deserve all seriousness. In this paper, we deliberate on the incredible possibilities that AI offers to forensic science as well as the challenges associated with it, from the standpoint that we are today poised at and where tomorrow is supposed to bring us for these potent instruments to aid and not undermine ‌justice.

items.title: AI and ML for Smart Cybersecurity and Digital Forensics
items.abstract: The rise of digital technologies crossing cloud computing, mobile computing, and device networking is not just bringing about novel opportunities but is also enabling cyberattacks of an incredibly high complexity level. Traditional security mechanisms based on static rules or human analysis have proven unable to detect highly advanced cyberattacks that are becoming increasingly difficult to trace. In this chapter, the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) as the most powerful methods for enhancing cyber security and conducting digital forensics is discussed. Ways of applying machine learning approaches, both classic algorithms and deep learning techniques, are described in terms of malware detection and identifying abnormal network activity. Additionally, the chapter illustrates the potential of artificial intelligence-enabled digital forensic solutions in surpassing the limitations of real-time defense mechanisms in performing activities such as automating the process of collecting evidence, reconstruction of logs, timeline analysis, communication analysis, and identification of manipulated media. The application of artificial intelligence in detecting phishing attacks is provided as an example that elaborates on how intelligent systems can play a pivotal role in enhancing the accuracy of identifying fraudulent emails. At the same time, the chapter mentions some of the challenges associated with the development of artificial intelligence technologies, which include adversarial manipulation, bias in training data, ethics-related concerns, the requirement for transparent AI models, among others, and outlines possible areas for future research.

items.title: AI at the Edge of Care
items.abstract: Modern healthcare is changing due to the quick development of wearable technology and smart sensing devices, which allow for continuous, real-time monitoring outside of traditional clinical settings. In order to provide prompt and individualized healthcare delivery, this chapter examines the new paradigm of edge-based artificial intelligence, which uses lightweight and resource-efficient models directly on wearable technology and smart sensors. In contrast to traditional cloud-centric methods, edge AI eliminates latency, improves data privacy, and lessens reliance on high-bandwidth connectivity, which makes it especially appropriate for vital health monitoring applications. The work provides a thorough overview of lightweight AI methods designed for contexts with limited resources, such as model compression, quantization, pruning, and TinyML. It also looks at how these methods can be integrated with smart biosensors for uses including activity recognition, early disease detection, cardiovascular monitoring, and remote patient care.

items.title: AI Bias in Special Education
items.abstract: Despite the rapid deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) to support K–12 educators in improving their practice, serious concerns remain unanswered about large-language model (LLM) output. This is especially true in special education, where educators report little training in disability theory, leading them to consult with AI systems without the background knowledge needed for objective analysis of the chatbot responses. To address this issue, we conducted a qualitative content analysis of the transcripts of responses from five major LLMs (Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, OpenAI ChatGPT, Perplexity Sonar, and xAI Grok) to common questions from early-career educators. We found an overreliance in the chatbot output on the Medical Model of disability, as well as almost no engagement with the Human Rights Model. We also found a wide variability between the different LLMs, as well as internal variability within each LLM based on the wording of the prompt. We conclude by calling for explicit instruction on disability theory in teacher preservice programs to support critical engagement by teachers with AI tools, as well as improved LLM models that consider multiple models of disability. This article makes a practical contribution to special education practice by identifying imbalanced AI output and suggesting ways to minimize the negative impacts that may result from using these tools.

items.title: AI Career Copilot: A Personalized Career Guidance and Skill Gap Analysis System
items.abstract: In today’s competitive job market, students and fresh graduates often face difficulties in selecting a suitable career and understanding the skills required to achieve their career goals. Many students are aware of job roles such as Software Developer, Data Analyst, Business Analyst, or Cybersecurity Engineer but are uncertain about the skills they currently possess, the skills they are missing, the correct learning sequence, and how to prepare for interviews. Existing career guidance platforms generally provide separate services such as job recommendations, learning resources, resume analysis, or interview preparation. This requires users to depend on multiple platforms and manually identify the gap between their current abilities and their desired career. The proposed project, “AI-Powered Career Guidance and Skill Gap Analysis System,” aims to provide an integrated solution to this problem through a web-based application developed using Python. The system allows users to either upload or paste their resume or directly enter their desired career goal, such as “I want to become a Software Developer.” The application uses Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to analyze the user's information and identify relevant technical skills, educational qualifications, projects, and other career-related information. The system compares the skills identified from the user's resume with the skills required for the selected career role..

items.abstract: With the increasing use of Artificial Intelligence tools and technologies among the young generation, we can observe that the use of AI tools and chatbots into day to day life has led many young individuals to seek emotional support and have more interaction on these platforms. Replika, Kuki etc. are some platforms that claim to be the AI companion “who cares for you” but as per various studies, they contribute to a higher sense of loneliness among people. According to a research study published in the International Journal of Human Computer Studies, a portion of the students on whom the study was conducted, were found seeking emotional support from AI chatbots. Apart from this, a 14 years old teen died by suicide after forming an attachment with an AI chatbot. This research aims to delve deeper into the paradox by examining the level or extent of young people’s reliance on such AI chatbots for emotional assistance and social interaction and how this dependence may unintentionally contribute to attachments with AI chatbots

items.title: AI driven oral cancer diagnosis from clinical imaging and computational pathology to precision therapeutics
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a computational approach for analysing the complex and heterogeneous data generated across oral cancer diagnosis and management. This narrative review provides an integrated overview of AI applications from early oral lesion detection, computational pathology, prognostic assessment, and precision therapeutics. It describes how machine learning and deep learning process clinical photographs, digitized histopathological images, whole-slide images, radiological examinations, and molecular or clinical data to generate task-specific outputs. The review covers AI-assisted identification of suspicious oral lesions, histopathological detection of oral epithelial dysplasia and oral squamous cell carcinoma, assessment of tumor differentiation, characterization of disease progression, and prediction of treatment response for therapeutic stratification. Particular attention is given to the relationship between the input data, computational task, and clinically relevant output rather than to model architecture alone. Although several studies report high diagnostic performance, much of the current evidence remains based on retrospective datasets and internal validation, while external, multicentre, and prospective evaluations are comparatively limited. Major challenges include dataset quality and representativeness, domain shift, annotation variability, interpretability, and integration into clinical workflows. Future progress will require patient-level evaluation, multicentre validation, multimodal integration, uncertainty-aware prediction, and prospective assessment of clinical utility. This review outlines the evolving role of AI as a potential decision-support framework across the oral cancer care pathway.

items.title: AI Powers Up Microgrids: An Optimization Revolution
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into microgrid systems is reshaping the way decentralized energy networks are monitored, optimized and sustained. During the last two decades fossil-fueled power stations have created destructive effects on electricity generation, thus demanding alternative power sources. Microgrids experience operational limitations during fault occurrences due to which they require dynamic energy management and optimization approaches to perform effectively. AI applications show increasing usefulness as a crucial element currently. Research examines detailed evaluations about how AI technologies optimize hybrid renewable microgrids in addition to enhancing power quality and analyzing fault conditions within microgrids. This research evaluates the application of machine learning (ML), genetic algorithms (GAs) and artificial neural networks (ANNs), fuzzy logic (FL), particle swarm optimization (PSO), heuristic optimization (HO), artificial bee colony (ABC) and other techniques for microgrid regulations, including classification and regression models. This study reviews microgrid applications of AI as well as future potential and their advantages alongside their limitations. The chapter investigates fault outbreak performance of renewable energy and wind and solar PV in coordinated operations that achieve maximum penetration levels within hybrid microgrids. This chapter provides an AI-based combined control system which optimizes energy distribution within multi-source microgrids through practical examples. At this stage AI applications demonstrate a quick pace of gaining importance. This research evaluates the applications of AI strategies on hybrid renewable microgrids for optimization and power quality improvements and fault outbreak analytics in microgrids. The two-layered control system improves decision efficiency through load forecasting by predicting simultaneous changes in power usage and power creation, especially in renewable environments with intermittent power sources such as solar and wind. The chapter investigates how intelligent algorithms work to reduce operational difficulties that include energy intermittency as well as fault detection and voltage instability and system disturbances. Real-world case studies and experimental outcomes help readers achieve practical understanding of how AI-powered microgrid management systems are put into practice and deliver their benefits. Finally, the use of AI in microgrid environments alongside their advantages and disadvantages and future opportunities are discussed. This study examines the maximum effective installation of renewable energy sources and both solar PV technology and wind power in hybrid microgrid systems as faults occur.

items.title: AI-Based Detection of Hallucinated Outputs in Chatbots Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Review and Conceptual Framework
items.abstract: Chatbots based on Large Language Models (LLMs) can provide quick, fluent, and informative answers, but they sometimes generate incorrect or unsupported information known as hallucinations. These hallucinations can reduce user trust and create problems in areas such as education, healthcare, research, and customer support. Therefore, detecting and preventing hallucinated outputs is important for developing reliable and trustworthy AI systems. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a useful approach that retrieves relevant information from trusted sources before generating an answer. This retrieved information can be used to check whether the chatbot's response is accurate and supported by available evidence. However, RAG alone cannot completely prevent hallucinations because the generated answer may still contain incorrect facts, irrelevant information, or unsupported statements. This paper proposes a conceptual framework for detecting hallucinations in chatbot responses by combining information retrieval, evidence-based verification, and rule-based validation. The system compares the generated answer with retrieved information and identifies statements that are incorrect or lack sufficient supporting evidence. Based on the verification results, the system classifies the response as reliable or flagged. If the response contains unsupported information, the system can suggest corrections or prevent the answer from reaching the user without proper verification. The proposed approach aims to improve answer accuracy, reduce misleading information, and increase transparency in AI-based conversational systems. Although this framework offers a promising direction, its effectiveness depends on the quality of retrieved information, verification methods, and decision thresholds. Future evaluation should measure detection accuracy, response time, and computational cost. This approach can support the development of safer, more reliable, and trustworthy chatbots across different application areas.

items.title: AI-Based Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models Learning: A Review
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can produce fluent but incorrect or fabricated statements, called hallucinations, which limits their use in education, healthcare and other high-stakes areas. Most existing safeguards act only after generation, and few correct errors automatically. This paper presents a structured narrative review of [N] verified sources published between [2022] and 2026, organized into seven themes: taxonomies, sampling-consistency detection, semantic-clustering methods, retrieval and fact-verification, internal-state detection, correction and integrated architectures, and evaluation practices. Black-box methods can detect hallucinations without external knowledge or model access, but only 8.8 % of reviewed systems combine detection and mitigation. Evidence relies heavily on question-answering benchmarks, small datasets, automatically generated labels and non-comparable metrics, and correction layers are rarely validated. The paper contributes a thematic synthesis, a comparison of [N] studies, a conceptual seven-layer self-correcting architecture and a prioritized research agenda.

items.title: AI-Based Intelligent Medical Report Understanding and Personal Health Management System
items.abstract: Medical reports contain important health information, but their technical terminology and numerical results may be difficult for patients to understand. Recent studies have explored the use of large language models to simplify radiology reports, while also identifying concerns related to accuracy, omitted information, and potentially misleading explanations [1–3]. This paper proposes an AI-Based Intelligent Medical Report Understanding and Personal Health Management System designed to make medical information easier to understand and organize. The proposed framework will accept medical reports in PDF or image format, extract relevant text, and generate patient-friendly explanations while aiming to preserve important values, units, and reference ranges. A retrieval-based component is proposed to support explanations using reliable medical sources. Additional planned features include date-wise health-record organization, comparison of comparable report values, and reminders based on user-entered or clinician-provided instructions. The framework emphasizes privacy, factual consistency, and the distinction between educational information and professional medical advice. Its evaluation will examine text-extraction accuracy, preservation of medical information, factual consistency, readability, and usability after implementation. As the system has not yet been experimentally evaluated, this paper presents the proposed design and evaluation plan rather than measured performance results.
